posts.message:
Tip: what a good missed-call text looks like.

1. Start with your business name.
2. Say why you're texting: "Sorry we missed your call."
3. Ask one simple question: "What's going on?"
4. Say how to stop: "Reply STOP to opt out."
5. Leave out coupons and sales pitches. A text-back is a reply, not an ad.

Short, polite, useful. See a full example: https://ailabpro.co/demo/

How it works, part 3: STOP.

If anyone replies STOP, QUIT, END, CANCEL, UNSUBSCRIBE, REVOKE or OPT OUT, the AI stops all automated texts to that number. The same goes for a sentence like "please stop texting me."

This check runs before the AI writes anything, and it covers reminders and confirmations too. If the person later texts START, they're back in.

More on how it works: https://ailabpro.co

posts.message:
Tip: when you book a job by text, offer two specific windows instead of asking "when works for you?"

"Tuesday 8 AM–12 PM or Tuesday 12–4 PM?" gets a one-word answer. An open question can start a back-and-forth that lasts all evening.

Same with the details: one question per text, starting with the ZIP code, so you know right away whether the job is in your area.

That's how our AI receptionist books: https://ailabpro.co/demo/

You decide which keywords count as urgent, and you can change them any time.

10 business days: the longest a business may take to honor a text opt-out under FCC rules in force since April 11, 2025 (47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10)). Replies like STOP, QUIT, END, CANCEL, UNSUBSCRIBE, REVOKE and OPT OUT all count.

If you text customers from a personal phone, someone has to remember who said stop.

Our AI receptionist stops all automated texts to a number as soon as that reply comes in. General information, not legal advice: https://ailabpro.co
